items.q: The prognosis written for bilateral RAS is:
opts: Responsive to PTRA alone without stenting

items.q: In bilateral RAS, loss of pressure natriuresis with ↓ RIHP leads to:
opts: ↑ Na+/H2O retention → intravascular volume overload → recurrent flash pulmonary edema
Sustained renin activation without volume change
items.exp: Loss of pressure natriuresis / ↓ RIHP → ↑ Na+/H2O retention → intravascular volume overload → recurrent flash pulmonary edema (d/t intravascular edema). (Book p751)

items.q: Which statement about the bilateral RAS diagram is TRUE?
opts: Intravascular volume overload feeds back negatively on the renin angiotensin system
The renin angiotensin system stays maximally stimulated without feedback
Pressure natriuresis is preserved in both kidneys
items.exp: The (−) arrow shows intravascular volume overload inhibiting the renin angiotensin system. (Book p751)

items.q: Recurrent flash pulmonary edema in bilateral RAS is treated with:
opts: B/L percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty with stenting
items.exp: Rx: B/L percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty with stenting. (Book p751)

items.q: For blood pressure control in bilateral RAS, the book lists diuretics as DOC while ACE inhibitors/ARBs are:
items.exp: In BP: diuretics (DOC); ACE inhibitors / ARBs: C/I as they ↓ GFR. (Book p751)

items.q: All of the following are listed in the bilateral RAS treatment block EXCEPT:
items.exp: Listed: diuretics (DOC), stop smoking, start statins; ACEi/ARBs are C/I. (Book p751)
